name: Read a brief
about: A deck, photos or notes become the asset list: every item the brief calls for, with the slide or photo it comes from, matched to the Library or marked missing. Each missing item has a Make button (Make an Object), and each made Object can be detailed next (Detail an Object). Since 2.0.0 Innowa reads it with you in the chat (R115) and asks what the brief leaves unclear.
useWhen: The owner has a brief (a deck, photos, drawings or notes) and wants the list of what it calls for, with what the Library already has and what is missing.

input.about: The brief: a deck (PDF), photos or drawings, and any notes. In a project, from its files; in the studio, added when you start the run (kept with the run).

rules.text: Every Need cites its evidence: the file and page (or photo) it came from, or the line of the notes.
Every Need gets one outcome with a reason: matched to a Library Object, an Object to adapt (with the parameters that change), or missing.

Agents never change the Library or a project's model. They write the run's Needs, matches and draft Objects; only the owner's decisions change anything: Keep (in a project) or Propose (in the studio, each Object by its own Propose to Library run and pull request).
Measure in millimetres. When a size is not given, use a usual size for the kind of thing and say so in the Need's notes.

steps.name: Read
steps.outcome: The brief becomes a list of Needs, each with its evidence.
instructions: Read the design brief and list its Needs: each distinct thing the space calls for that the Library could supply (furniture, fixtures, columns and other placeable things), not rooms, finishes or services.
Read every file of the brief with the Read tool (PDF pages and images too) and the owner's notes: step_get lists them, and the chat's step note gives where each is.
One Need per distinct thing: a name a designer would use ("3-seat sofa, grey fabric"), the quantity, sizes in mm when given, and notes on look and material.
Evidence is required: the file and page ("deck.pdf p. 4"), the photo ("living.jpg") or "notes" with the words quoted.

For each Need also write seen: what you saw at its evidence, in one sentence a maker could work from (the look, the material, how it opens, anything the size alone doesn't say). The next step, and the Objects made after, work from it.

Save the whole list with needs_put (calling it again replaces the list). Tell the owner in one or two sentences how many Needs you found, and ask about anything the brief leaves unclear that changes the list (a quantity, which of two options) rather than guessing.

steps.name: Match
steps.outcome: Every Need is matched to a Library Object, an Object to adapt, or marked missing, with a reason.
instructions: Match each Need to the Library. run_state gives the Needs with their evidence and what was seen; library_list gives every Library Object in a line; call library_get for each one you consider. Open a Need's page or photo with Read when the words aren't enough.

For each Need choose one: "object" (a Library Object fits as it is, within its parameter limits: give the parameter values), "adapt" (a Library Object is close but needs changes beyond its limits or a different look: say which), or "missing" (nothing in the Library is that kind of thing).
Give a reason a designer would accept, in one sentence. Do not stretch a match: a dining chair is not an office chair.

Save all matches at once with matches_put (calling again replaces them). Tell the owner in one sentence how many matched, need adapting and are missing; the asset list on the run page then has a Make button for each missing one.

output.name: Asset list
output.about: Every item the brief calls for with its evidence, what it matched in the Library, and a Make button for each missing one.
